attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The Bing anecdote is context; the claim is his own description of GPT.

semantics.note: The normalised wording matches the sentence. It is a present-tense description of the GPT systems of the time.

contract.note: Reading 'not smart enough to filter out falsehood' as unreliable screening, not total inability, is the ordinary and fair reading. Limiting it to March to April 2023 matches the post's frame.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own release notes admit GPT-4 still hallucinates facts. This works against OpenAI's interest. Its reported gains in factuality do not show reliable screening.
Volokh, March 2023: GPT-4 produced misconduct allegations and quotes his searches could not find. These are documented false outputs with reputational risk.

reviews.rationale: Records from the time show GPT-4 inventing allegations and quotes about misconduct, and OpenAI admitted it was unreliable on facts. That meets the support condition under the fair reading of unreliable screening. OpenAI's reported improvements do not show reliable screening, so the contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I don't doubt... will' is a firm expectation, so this is a scored forecast. No deadline was given.

contract.note: In context, 'defense and security' means military and national security: the paragraph covers China, the defense department, and air forces. Counting commercial brand-protection and in-house code scanning stretches the speaker's meaning, and that stretch decides the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI describing a customer's commercial brand-threat pipeline. It is a company disclosure, not national defense or security, and gives no independent measure of GPT-5's effect.
OpenAI's own announcement that a GPT-5-powered agent found vulnerabilities. This is self-reported commercial cybersecurity, not a defense or national-security effect.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The only evidence is OpenAI's own reports of commercial cybersecurity use. On the reading the context supports (military and national security), the packet itself says no effect was established. No conclusive event is shown, so the forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective statement about his own predictions.

semantics.note: The wording keeps both universal claims. The 'Marcus says' framing is awkward but does not change the commitment.

contract.note: Requiring a check of the full list of predictions, and not counting still-open long-term forecasts as wrong, is fair to the universal wording.

evidence.note: Marcus's December 2022 essay. It shows what he predicted, not whether the predictions came true. It is his own writing, despite the 'secondary summary' label.
OpenAI's own release notes confirm hallucinations and reasoning errors persisted. This covers only some of the predicted flaws.

reviews.rationale: Only the hallucination and reasoning-error predictions are confirmed. The packet does not check downstream integration, guardrails, alignment, the other items, or the full list of predictions. The universal claim is neither established nor refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The wording keeps both the weak-play claim and the comparison to 1978 chess computers.

contract.note: Judging full games by GPT-4 without an engine, and requiring rough parity with representative 1978 machines, is an ordinary reading. Marcus named no machine or tolerance.

evidence.note: One GPT-4 game from March 2023 with blunders and then illegal moves. It supports weak play in that game only and says nothing about the 1978 comparison.
The author's two GPT-4 games had illegal moves, but he calls the data too limited. The 1402 rating is for GPT-3.5.

reviews.rationale: The evidence is one recorded game plus an anecdote about two more. That is too thin to show general playing strength. Possible counter-accounts could not be read, and there is no 1978 baseline, so neither part is settled under the contract.
